title: Land Cover Shapes Altitudinal Land Surface Warming Patterns Across Switzerland
content:
Abstract

Mountainous regions are characterized by steep vertical gradients in temperature which in turn shape land cover and ecosystems that are differently affected by climate change. Here, we show that both stable and changing land covers have an important influence on land surface temperature (LST) trends in Switzerland, based on almost four decades of high-resolution data across the entire country. Warming is consistently highest in settlements and agricultural areas and substantially reduced where vegetation is abundant. The most pronounced relative LST increases are due to glacier retreat, followed by urbanization, whereas increases in vegetation cover induce relative cooling. These land-cover dynamics impose a distinct altitudinal structure on LST trends that is further intensified by changing snow regimes. Collectively, land-cover change has imposed additional warming beyond that associated with stable land-cover conditions. These results highlight land-cover dynamics as a critical determinant of mountain surface warming.
